name: Plum
grown_as: Fruit trees on rootstocks: 'Victoria' (two), 'Opal' (dwarf) and 'Warwickshire Drooper'. 'Victoria' fruit is pinky red over yellow, 'Opal' red-purple, 'Warwickshire Drooper' yellow. The drawing shows a 'Victoria'-type red-purple plum.
habit: A small deciduous tree with a rounded, spreading crown, 3 to 5 m on St Julien A or Pixy rootstock. Dark brown-grey bark with pale horizontal lines (lenticels). 'Warwickshire Drooper' has weeping branches. Fruits on spurs and on one-year-old wood.

leaf.outline: Elliptic to obovate (widest a little above the middle), 4 to 10 cm long
leaf.margin: Finely and bluntly toothed all round, the teeth rounded and often in pairs
leaf.veins: A midrib and 5 to 8 pairs of side veins, with a fine net between them beneath
leaf.surface: Dull, slightly wrinkled dark green above; paler and downy beneath, especially along the veins
leaf.stalk: Short, 1 to 2 cm, downy, often with one or two tiny glands near the top

flower.centre: Twenty to thirty long stamens with yellow anthers around a single green style
flower.behind: Five small green sepals, often bent back
flower.carried: One to three together on short stalks (1 to 2 cm) straight from buds on the spurs and old wood, crowding along the branches, opening just before or with the leaves

fruit: A drupe with a single stone: oval, 3 to 7 cm, with a shallow groove (the suture) down one side and a pale waxy bloom that rubs off. 'Victoria' pinky red speckled over yellow; others purple, red or yellow. Hangs on a short stalk, often several along a branch. Ripe August to September. Fruit set: small green oval fruitlets, at first carrying the dry remains of the flower.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as grafted trees
winter: Bare tree. Dark grey-brown branches with short spurs carrying clusters of small, round flower buds; small pointed leaf buds on the shoots.

leaf: simple leaf widest above the middle with a wedge base
dull, slightly wrinkled surface with the vein net showing
bloom: many stamens with yellow anthers around ONE style, not five
young: a single trunk with spreading branches
dormant: bare dark branches with short spurs
clusters of small round flower buds on the spurs
flower: small white flowers crowded along the branches in ones to threes
flowers on short stalks, opening just before or with the first leaves
set: small green oval fruitlets on short stalks along the branches
crop: oval fruit with a groove down one side and a waxy bloom
fruit hanging on short stalks along the branches

look_alikes: Damson and bullace are smaller-fruited forms of the same species. Blackthorn (Prunus spinosa) is spiny, flowers on bare black twigs well before the leaves and has small blue-black sloes. Cherry plum (Prunus cerasifera) flowers earlier, in March, with glossy leaves and round fruit. Cherries carry their flowers in bunches on long stalks.
